usage: Four quadrant atlases: primary floor, secondary floor, wall, detail. Runtime texture sampling only.
prompts: Create a production-ready material texture atlas for a top-down 2D game set in a Japanese public building. Square image, exactly four equal square quadrants arranged 2 by 2, with NO gutters, NO labels, NO text, NO objects, NO perspective, NO lighting gradients. Each quadrant is a perfectly flat orthographic seamless repeating material swatch. Upper left: realistic warm ivory terrazzo floor, fine cream aggregate, subtle well-maintained wear. Upper right: pale beige ceramic square floor tiles with fine gray grout, four-by-four tiles within the quadrant. Lower left: desaturated teal painted plaster wall, fine realistic tactile microtexture and subtle wear, evenly colored. Lower right: light gray stone and concrete wall material, evenly lit, fine granular realism. Soft diffuse neutral light, subtle believable realism, restrained contrast so tiny black stick-figure characters are readable over it. All materials cropped right to quadrant boundaries, no frames, no 3D depth, no props, no logos. Not a game screenshot: this is a reusable texture atlas used inside the actual game. Resolution at least 1024x1024.

Japanese school: upper left warm honey oak planks with delicate woodgrain and subtle polish; upper right muted warm beige linoleum floor with fine speckles; lower left pale sage green painted plaster wall; lower right cream ceramic bathroom tile with fine grout. Calm well-maintained nostalgic school materials, not dirty horror.
